Whether you're brand new to the SCA and curious about how it all works, or a seasoned member looking to pick up a new skill or give back to your group, Allthing has something for you. A major focus of the day is pulling back the curtain on how the SCA runs. We'll have officer classes and training sessions to help you understand what our officers do and what it takes to step into those roles. Interested in serving your local group but not sure where to start? This is the perfect place to find out. Beyond that, expect a full day of classes and workshops covering everything from martial activities to hospitality, with plenty of opportunities learn new skills and meet the folks that keep the dream alive. A potluck lunch will be held in the hall — bring a dish to share and enjoy good food and great company. This event is free and open to all. No experience necessary — just bring your curiosity and be ready to have fun!

description: Come join us at Carolingian Dance Practice! The winter/spring 2026 practices will be on fourth Tuesdays: Feb 24, Mar 24, Apr 28, May 26, and June 23rd. This is a fun social occasion for all: an evening where we all get together to learn Renaissance Dances and socialize with the members of the Barony. It is specifically newcomer-friendly: all dances are taught, you don’t need to come with a partner (we encourage folks to switch partners from dance to dance), and folks generally come in street clothes. Just wear something comfortable that you can move in (especially comfortable shoes). We meet from 7:30 – 9:30pm at the Holy Trinity Armenian Church, at 145 Brattle Street in Cambridge. There’s a parking lot for those who need to drive, bus routes nearby, and it’s less than a 20 minute walk from the Harvard Square MBTA station. The parking lot is off of Sparks Street, on the far side of the Church away from Brattle Street. (If using a GPS, 62 Sparks Street is roughly across the street from the parking lot.) The hall where we will be dancing is next to the parking lot, so if you are walking up Brattle Street, turn onto Sparks Street to get to the hall. If the front door on Sparks Street is locked, come around to the parking lot side and use the door there. Dances are taught and called using the gender-free “Larks and Robins” style, popular with many of the local dance communities. We have a lot of space (easily twice what we need for dancing), so folks are welcome to come bring other SCA activities for the sidelines, or even to just come hang out! The site costs $100 per session; donations are optional, but welcome to help defray the cost of renting the hall. So come join us! It’s very much “the more, the merrier”, and you’re very welcome to join in!

title: Festival of the Rose (Dun Or)
location: 41337 10th St W, Palmdale, CA 93551, USA
description: Unto the Good People of Caid, warm Greetings and most gracious Salutations! The Barony of Dun Or joyfully invites one and all to join us for a day of mirth, merriment and noble fellowship at the Festival of the Rose, to be held upon Saturday, the Fifteenth of August 2026. Come and join us in a splendid celebration of love, beauty, and the Arts and Artisans of glorious Caid, held in honor of Her Royal Majesty, our radiant and most beloved Queen Fara! The noble tradition of the Festival of the Rose first blossomed in the year 1980 as the Queen’s Arts Tea, when Her Royal Majesty Amsha called upon the Chivalry and the Royal Guard to display their skill and talents in honor of the occasion, and in tribute to the Crown. In that same spirit of inspiration, Her Majesty, Queen Fara, most warmly invites and encourages all associates to the Peerage — Squires, Apprentices, Protégés, Provosts, and Prodigies alike — together with all artisans, scholars, and performers throughout the realm, to present the fruits of their skill and imagination in the Arts, Sciences, and the Bardic traditions. Whether set forth for admiration or entered in honorable competition, let all works be offered in celebration of Her Majesty and in pursuit of the title of Her Champion. And should you have need of treasures rare and wondrous, rejoice! A silent auction will be held for the benefit of the Kingdom Travel Fund! If you are interested in gifting the auction with any treasures - in good condition, of course- that you may no longer need, please bring them for inclusion, or email a detailed gift certificate to Her Royal Majesty's Chamberlain, Duchess Lorissa, at ! We look forward to celebrating Beauty, Love, and Our Beloved Queen Fara with you at the Festival of the Rose! SCHEDULE: 8:30am - Site opens for Artisans to set up displays 9am - Site opens for all other attendees 10am - Opening Court, or at Their Majesties' pleasure. 12pm - Lunch 1pm - Bardic Performances begin, or at Their Majesties' pleasure 4pm - Closing Court 5pm - Site closes EVENT REGISTRATION: Adult Event Registration $25, Adult Member Discount Event Registration, $15. Youth aged 17 and under are guests of the Barony. Acceptable payment forms: Please make checks payable to SCA, Inc/Barony of Dun Or. We will gratefully accept donations at the gate to offset the cost of Non-Member Surcharges for gentles who may have need, especially guests that may be attending their first event. A&S Competition/Displays: Artisans are encouraged to provide A&S demonstrations throughout the day. Please submit this sign-up form if you would like to compete or display your A&S: Performance Arts: Do you have a song to sing? A rhyme to rhyme? A story to tell? Happy feet that simply *must* dance in honor of Her Majesty? If so, you are welcome to do so during our Performance Art Presentations! All performances should be limited to 2-5 minutes, and will be scheduled throughout the day! To claim your spot for a bardic performance, please sign up at: by NO LATER THAN AUGUST 10 at 11:59 PM. For questions, or more information, please contact our Performance Arts Coordinator, His Excellency Baron Fadi! Classes: Do you know something really cool? Only know a little bit about it? You do not need to be an expert to share your interests. Please submit below to teach a class. Site information/Restrictions: No smoking or vaping inside or within 25 feet of playgrounds, observe all signage. No alcoholic entries. Service animals always welcome. Leashed Pets outside ok. In accordance with the SCA core value of respecting the worth and dignity of all individuals and the desire to promote an environment safe for our youngest participants, we kindly ask that artisans and bardic displays meet the requirements of the values of our hosts, and do not include vulgar, violent and/ or sexual content. Event Stewards: Dueña Tsura Romani Event Email: -caid.org Directions: CA-14 N or S to W Ave N/Avenue N in Palmdale. Take exit 39 from CA-14 N Continue on W Ave N/Avenue N to 10 th Street West, turn left (northbound) onto 10 th west from Ave N. Your destination is on the left. (East side of 10 th st w)

description: Hosted by: Kaarnemaa | EN/FI/SWE Rajataverna - Gränstavernan 30.7-2.8.2026 Again, the northern medieval and Iron Age folk will gather on the border and welcome all travelers from near and far! This will be the first time the Tavern will be located in Finland. The site is a hunting lodge 10 km from the Swedish border. The event will be a relaxed reenactment event, which is open to new and old historical reenactors. The event is organized by the Peräpohjolan keskiaikaseura which is part of the international Society for Creative Anachronism and Suomen keskiaikaseura (The medieval society of Finland). In the terms of the Society: The village of Torna in Aarnimetsä, Drachenwald. We are even collaborating with Frostheim (Luleå) from the principality of Nordmark (Sweden) and are officially sponsored by Kaarnemaa (Oulu) from Aarnimetsä. Although Rajataverna / Gräsntavernan is a SCA-event, you do not need to be a member of the society in order to participate! Rajataverna is a place for everyone to meet regardless of any borders. The event languages are Finnish, Swedish and English. The program is currently under construction and we are looking for teachers in Arts & Sciences, fighting, etc. If you want to teach, let us know! There will be a homely feast and a small market, where you can bring new and second hand items. The program is updating all the time and the final schedule will be published well before the event. It is possible to arrive at the site on Friday 17 o’clock and the event site must be empty by midday on Sunday. Please note that Rajataverna is living in Finnish time due to its location. The hunting lodge Tapiolan maja has cabins for 24 persons. You are free to bring your own tent and we will create a crash space if needed. The lodge has a sauna and a fireplace. Whole weekend (includes accommodation & food) 40 € / 440 kr SCA-members 45 € / 470 kr non-members 20 € / 210 kr minors Children under 7 are free Day visit on Saturday (includes food) 15 € / 170 kr for an adult 10 € / 110 kr children over 7 years The meals include snacks on Friday evening, breakfast, lunch and feast on Saturday and breakfast on Sunday. People coming from outside the Nordics can pay at the door. Payment information will be sent later via email. Please note that the event is inclusive and we actively work towards a safe environment to have fun in. If you are interested, but new to reenactment, you can contact the event organizer for help. title: Royal Archer Tournament (Bright Hills)
location: Baltimore Bowmen, 10301 Harford Rd, Glen Arm, MD, 21057
description: Join us for a day of fun and archery! Come out and shoot at strange and magical creatures. Bring lots of arrows! Most stations will require 8 arrows/bolts be shot and/or a long timed end. If you are shooting to win, be sure to be on site and inspected prior to morning court as the clout will be shot immediately after and will not be run again. No loaner equipment will be provided, so be sure to bring your own, or get in contact with someone to bring theirs to lend to you. A prize will be given to someone that can guess the theme of the shoot and where these creatures came from and can be won by non- archers as well. There will be lots of other prizes to be won as well by the archers. The top rank of each royal round class will have a medal that they can take home with them, it will need to be returned for the following year. Additional prizes will be announced later. As customary with the Royal Archery competition, there will be a 16-person shoot-off at the end to announce the Royal Archer Champion. The person that wins this will be able to place their coat of arms on the Royal Archer Quiver and will be in charge of putting the shoot together for the following year. For those that won a medal for their ranking in 2025, please get in contact with Chris LeStrange to return it so that we can pass it on to the new winners this year. You can contact him at ChrisRStrange@gmail.com.

description: Come celebrate the East Kingdom's oldest shire as we turn 50! This will be a Full weekend of events with a magical feast! We open Friday night with a potluck Tavern night with a hafla and music. Saturday we will have heavy fighting, fencing, archery, thrown weapons; Arts & Sciences classes & displays. Guild meetings for Blacksmiths, soothsayers, and foresters! Sunday we will have our usual Shire martial championships. We welcome Merchants to come sell their wares with no booth charge. We will be having an amazing feast Saturday night with culinary dishes from around the world and across times! Pre-reg is required to get on board for it. After Feast Saturday night, we will be having a Tudor/Elizabethan dessert board with dancing and revelry. Camping, bunks and tenting all available Site Opens: 12 Noon on Friday Site Closes: 6p Sunday

description: For Twelfth Night 2027, the populace is invited to celebrate a season of transition, where old traditions and joyful excess meet at the turning of the year. The theme draws inspiration from late medieval southern Germany and Switzerland, where winter observances blended seamlessly with lively seasonal celebrations marking the close of one cycle and the promise of the next. By the fifteenth century, these celebrations had fused into a distinctive blend of formality and fun. Daytime brought courtly pomp, displays of skill, and structured ceremony, while nightfall ushered in feasting, dancing, and masked revelry. This balance of order and exuberance provides the perfect setting for Atlantia’s Twelfth Night, offering a full day of pageantry and arts followed by an evening devoted to celebration, community, and unapologetic joy. During this time, the days surrounding Twelfth Night marked the end of the winter holiday season and the gradual shift toward spring. Communities gathered for pageantry, symbolic acts of renewal, and public festivities that reflected both reflection and anticipation. These moments were as much about community and tradition as they were about marking time itself. Alongside this came Fasnacht, a vibrant pre Lenten carnival that preserved much older seasonal customs. Masquerades, mummers, and playful processions filled towns with music, laughter, and satire. Masks and costumes allowed for mischief and creativity, and the rules of everyday life were happily bent before the long quiet of late winter.

There is no lifeguard on duty, and river conditions (including currents, depth, temperature, and debris) can change quickly and without warning. All individuals who choose to access the river do so at their own risk. Children must be directly supervised by a responsible adult at all times. description: Let the word spread far and wide, Whipping Winds is upon us! There are rustlings north of the border!! A voice on the wind calls “we’re not dead yet, eh!” Travel to the Northern Realms for the last celebration of the summer season! Join the Shire of Windegate at Williamson Park in Shelby Montana and celebrate in jubilant Northern style as Hordes from Avacal cross the border once again to celebrate our friendship. We hope! Fighting, Archery, Thrown Weapons, Dancing and Music, Arts and Classes, and Shopping! All are to be found in abundant supply amongst the trees along the shore of the Marias River. Before we batten down the hatches for the long nights of winter, the Kingdoms of Artemisia and Avacal shall join together on the fields of battle, and around the campfires beneath the stars, to solidify our mutual respect and kinship. The Autocrat team is planning activities for full days of merriment and contests! There will be Armored battles, on the main field, and into the woods! Don’t forget our Founder's Battle, and Sir Terrell’s booty tournament. Rapier will also have battle scenes and tournaments to determine who is the best. For the Arts & Sciences minded persons, we are planning to have classes, and display for your projects. Archery is a mainstay at this event, and there will be animal targets, Royal Rounds, and three archery championships. There will be organized children activities, and hopefully a practice of Youth Combat! Both Friday and Saturday nights, we will be hosting Haflas and Games for all to enjoy! SITE: Williamson Park, {72 Williamson Park Road, Shelby MT 59474} Gate opens Thursday at 12:00 noon, August 13th and closes Sunday at 12:00 noon, August 16th. The site is south of Shelby Montana, on the Marias River. At this time of year, the Marias is a wonderfully slow-moving river that has room for wading & swimming. Parents are asked to keep a mindful eye on their children. There are shade trees, an area for RV’s, a permanent playground, and a permanent building for toilets & fresh water. Fire restrictions will be dependent on Seasonal USFS restrictions. Pets allowed, on leash. FEES: Adults {age 18 years +} event registration fee for the weekend: $35.00 USD. Adult member registration for the weekend: $25.00 USD Children, age 17 and younger are guests of the shire. Day trip fees for Friday or Saturday $25 each day; Membership registration $15.00 each day. Make checks payable to Shire of Windegate DIRECTIONS: Take your best route on I-15 to Shelby Montana. Take exit 358 and follow the road south 1 mile to Williamson Park Road. Turn left {east). This will be a dirt road. Signs will be posted to guide travelers. If you cross the river, you have gone too far. Shelby is 7 miles north of the site, and has groceries, gas, hotels and other necessities. GPS: 48 25’ 31.90” N, 111 52’ 33.44” W Event Steward:Freydis Bjarnarsdottir fallenmum@gmail.com Knight Marshal: HE Sir Terrell al-Qasab the Butcher dabucha@3rivers.net

title: 👑🌹 🤴👸Kings Road - Everyone
location: Swift River Ranch, 4313 Duck Creek Rd, Billings, MT 59101
description: King's Road returns for its third year as Artemisia's premier event, a great gathering where we celebrate the myriad of endeavors that bring us together in the spirit of these Current Middle Ages. Full schedules of armored and rapier melees and tournaments, thrown weapons, equestrian, and more archery than you can shake a stick at! There's a Laurel’s Prize Tourney, Classes, Merchants, Parties, and Dances. Baronial and Royal Courts. A full suite of youth activities, including social gatherings, construction workshops, archery, thrown weapons, and youth combat. Truly, something for everyone! This year, we'll be continuing with a full-fledged MENAT area for classes, activities, parties, music, lectures, and more specific to the history of pre-16th C. Middle East, North Africa, and Turkey. To help folks get to and from all the venues within the site, our golf cart transport system is being continued. Our site is shaded with grass and trees and has a large building we will use for court, classes, and revelry. Above-ground fire pits are welcomed. The days are long but not too hot, and the nights are cool and filled with the scents of summer. The site is damp, and we encourage responsible merrymaking. Those planning to bring horses should contact the Kingdom Equestrian Deputy at equestrian@artemisia.sca.org to coordinate. Because this is a working ranch, no pets are allowed. Group camps must register as such to receive a land allocation. Preregistration is strongly encouraged. RV spots are available by reservation (no hookups). Please visit the website for details. A special Noon to 5pm Saturday Day Fee will be offered at no cost, to allow people unfamiliar with the SCA to come and visit an SCA event. Please note this is not a demo. All participants at King’s Road must make an attempt at pre-17th century dress, and must sign or have waivers on file. A Loaner Garb Booth will be available during the no-fee period for those needing period clothing, along with a quick primer and tours on how to attend an SCA event. Site opens: 10am Wednesday, June 17 Site closes: Noon Sunday, June 21 Location: Swift River Ranch, 4313 Duck Creek Rd, Billings, MT 59101 Directions: Take I-90 to exit 443 (Zoo Drive) between Laurel and Billings, Montana, turning south off the interstate. Turn right onto South Frontage Road and go 2.1 miles. Turn left onto Duck Creek Road. After 1.2 miles, the road will curve right. Continue, and take the next left to remain on Duck Creek Road, crossing the river. Swift River Ranch will be on your left. This activity will be held Friday afternoon before Court. The teams will consist of one Heavy, one Rapier, one Archer, one assassin (thrown weapons) and one optional runner. Each team must have one woman and one child aged 17 or younger, no Timmer, this is not you. We are proud to announce the return of His Excellency Master Reynhard Sebastian Von Reutte's FRIDAY NIGHT FIGHTS for another year!! Warriors choose your battle songs now! Those who neglect this important function will have a song chosen for them. By default, this will be the Chicken Dance Song or some other equally embarrassing musical offering. Landed Baronesses may sponsor 3 fighters, Former Landed Baroness may sponsor 2 fighters and Court Baronesses may sponsor 1 fighter. It is recommended that fighters bring a token of appreciation in gratitude for their Baroness allowing them to carry their favor into battle. There will also be the Black Knight Melee following the Thistle and Sage Tourney. The ONLY acceptable target hits will be arms and legs (within the rules of engagement outlined within the Kingdom Marshals Handbook). The Baron Thomas Memorial Tournament (thrown weapons) and Archery Tournaments will run concurrent to the Black Knight Melee. These will also be the Baronial Championship Tournaments. Following the Black Knight Melee will be the Baroness’s Target Practice, wherein all warriors will present themselves at the Castle wall to be taunted and skewered by arrows. All voice heralds are called to the Castle walls for the taunting of the targets (you can win prize!!) Open range time for Archery and thrown weapons will be at the discretion of the Marshals. Additional Melee events will be at the discretion of His Majesty . Additional information: Trash will be self clean up. Please haul your trash out when you leave site. Please also include your camp dimensions with your Preregistration so that we can make sure we have best use of available land, or have your Camp Coordinator reach out to our Land Steward. See Kingdom Events for Pre-Registration information and updates on schedules and activities. Equestrian events are currently in the planning stages. See event page for updates.
